newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone firm after ceo comment, BZW "buy".
newsitem.headline: Vodafone firm after ceo comment, BZW "buy".

text.p: Shares in Vodafone Plc held steady in a sharply falling UK equity market on Friday as analysts at BZW raised estimates on the stock after upbeat comment to U.S. investors this week by chief executive Chris Gent, dealers said.
Vodafone shares were unchanged at 277p by 1344 GMT in active trade of 4.2 million shares, even as the FTSE 100 index was down 48.8 points at 4,223.1.

Interviewed on Thursday after a breakfast meeting with investors, Gent told Reuters he was "not uncomfortable" with current analyst estimates, which see pre-tax profit growth of some 20 percent in fiscal 1998.

Sources said BZW analysts repeated a "buy" on Vodafone and raised their pre-tax profit estimate for the year ending March 1998 to 600 million stg from 570 million. Analysts at the brokerage were not immediately available for comment.

Vodafone shares rose earlier this week as the company said its international subscriber numbers passed one million for the first time. Separately Merrill Lynch raised its price target on the stock to 300p.
Gent took over from Sir Gerry Whent as chief executive of Vodafone on January 1 and kicked off a round of investor meetings in the U.S. this week.
